editorial:
Imagine a movie where the director plays himself and spends the whole time arguing with his favorite actor. You get to step into the world of Yehia, a famous Egyptian filmmaker who is totally obsessed with a handsome young man named Amr. He wants Amr to be his star in every single project, but the two of them have very different ideas about art. It feels like a long, colorful conversation about fame, love, and the struggle to make something great. The vibe is very artistic and personal, almost like you are peaking into a real diary of a man who cannot let go of his dreams.

You will love how the movie jumps between different movie sets, from a serious play like Hamlet to a big musical about Alexander the Great. The acting is very natural and feels like a real friendship that is slowly falling apart. One downside is that it can feel a bit slow if you are looking for a traditional plot with a clear beginning and end. However, if you like stories about creative people, you should definitely check it out. You can find it for rent on Apple TV, but for the best colors and sound, you might want to add the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection.
endingExplained: The story wraps up as Yehia finally realizes that he cannot control Amr or force him to be exactly who he wants. After all the fighting and failed movie ideas, there is a feeling of acceptance. Yehia stops trying to mold the young actor into a perfect version of himself. It ends with a sense of peace, showing that their bond is more important than any movie script or fame they could achieve together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about artists and complicated friendships.
